entry.author: Climate Change Commission
entry.summary:
Every six years, the Commission publishes a national climate change risk assessment - identifying the most significant climate related risks for Aotearoa New Zealand, and where focused and coordinated action would make the biggest difference. This webinar provides an overview of our 2026 assessment from Karen Lavin (General Manager, Evidence and Advice) and Holly Walker (Project Director).

Explore the risk assessment, supporting evidence, case studies and more on our website: https://www.climatecommission.govt.nz/nccra-2026

Our slides from this presentation are available on our website: https://www.climatecommission.govt.nz/webinars

CHAPTERS:

Karen Lavin (General Manager, Evidence and Advice)
00:20 Why this work is important
01:55 Purpose of the assessment
03:46 What the assessment provides

Holly Walker (Project Director)
05:06 How we assessed the risks
11:01 Examples of risk and domain scorecards
12:09 The ten most significant climate risks
14:13 Risks to Key infrastructure; Risks to Communities and safety
18:35 Risks to Nature and the bioeconomy; Risks to Decisions and funding
22:35 Navigating the future
24:23 Supporting material and evidence
25:38 Key takeaways

Q&A
27:56 How was cascading risk assessed? What method was used to score them?
30:17 What will central government do with this information?
31:41 Biogeophysical and biogeochemical systems as part of the natural environment domain
33:03 What advice would you give for enabling action on these risks whilst in an election year?
34:13 Are there resources for communicating this work to the general public?
35:50 Is there collaboration happening between teams doing these risk assessments in other countries?
37:48 Are there plans to look at transitional risks in moving to a low emissions economy?
39:23 Do you have any engagement and workshops planned with local government on this assessment?
40:41 Are severity, readiness and cascading risk all rated equally, or are they weighted?
42:12 How might this work inform a national energy strategy that is more resilient to climate change?
44:07 What were the biggest methodological challenges?
46:58 How would you recommend applying the findings at a district level?
48:38 Interest from the business sector on this kind of risk assessment
50:11 How do New Zealand's risks compare to other countries?
